### Fixed

  • Release builds no longer carry code-coverage instrumentation that writes default.profraw when the bundled command or server exits. Release gates now inspect the finished binaries and exercise CLI/server execution without coverage output redirection.
  • Help now opens an offline copy of this app's user manual, including the corrected command-line session documentation, shipped with the app.

Unison UI for macOS 0.10.0

Version 0.10.0 completes how a unison <profile> request behaves when the app is already running. A request now carries its own command-line options to the running instance, waits for the app when it is busy instead of being turned away, and, when a synchronization is in progress, asks you how to handle it. Existing profiles and settings continue to work without migration.

Added

  • Options are delivered to the running instance. unison <profile> -path <dir> handed to a running app opens that profile scoped to <dir>, exactly as the same command would at a fresh launch. -include and -source are carried too, with order, repeated options, and profile precedence preserved. How the running app was itself started no longer matters: each request is scoped only by its own options.
  • A busy app makes the request wait instead of turning it away. If the app is scanning, showing reconciliation results, or finishing a previous run, it accepts the request and opens the profile once that work and its cleanup finish. The command reports that it was accepted and is waiting, and the app shows it waiting.
  • A request during a synchronization asks how to handle the sync. When a sync is running, the app raises its Keep Syncing / Abort & Close / Close (let it run) decision for the requested profile. The command prints that a synchronization is running and a decision is required in the app, then waits for your choice within a short window: stopping the sync or letting it finish in the background opens the requested profile; Keep Syncing leaves the sync untouched and does not open it. No command ever aborts a sync or makes that choice on its own.

Changed

  • A request to a busy app is no longer simply refused. Earlier versions kept the work in progress and told you they did not start the new profile. Now the request waits (for a scan or cleanup) or asks you how to handle a running sync, and opens the profile when it can. The profile editor and a recovery/restart state still refuse, with a specific reason and the step to take.

Notes

  • Only one command-line request is handled at a time. A second request while one is waiting is refused with a clear message, and choosing a profile in the app never silently replaces a waiting command-line request.
  • If a request cannot be confirmed (the reply was lost), the command says so and asks you to check the app before running it again, rather than retrying on its own; the original request may already have been accepted.

Unison UI for macOS 0.9.0

Version 0.9.0 makes the app's unison command open the graphical app by default and act on a profile you name. When you run unison <profile> without choosing an interface, it now follows a Default interface preference that is Graphical unless you set it to Text, and a graphical launch opens that profile and starts its connection and scan right away. Existing profiles and settings continue to work without migration.

Added

  • Default interface for the unison command (Settings ▸ Command Line). A Graphical or Text control sets which interface unison uses when a command omits -ui. It defaults to Graphical, so typing unison <profile> opens this app. An explicit -ui graphic or -ui text always overrides the preference.
  • A profile on the command line opens and scans. In graphical mode, unison <profile> opens the app and starts that profile's connection and scan right away, without a further click. It stops at the reconciliation results, so nothing is applied until you act.
  • Requests reach a running instance. When the app is already running, unison <profile> is handled by that instance instead of starting a second one: it opens the profile when idle at the picker, and keeps its work and reports a clear refusal when a scan, reconciliation, sync, or a profile edit is in progress. The command returns a matching exit status.

Changed

  • A bare unison <profile> now opens the app by default. Earlier versions ran Unison's text interface when -ui was omitted; the default is now Graphical for every account without a saved preference. If you relied on the text interface from a bare unison <profile>, set Default interface to Text in Settings ▸ Command Line, or pass -ui text.

Notes

  • Scripts and scheduled jobs should pass -ui text explicitly rather than depend on the default interface. With the Graphical default in effect, a headless unison <profile> (over ssh, from cron, or from launchd, with no graphical session) is refused with a message instead of running in the terminal.
